claim: The Namur cable car (Téléphérique) departs from Place Maurice Servais and runs to the Citadel; one-way adult fare €5.50, return €8.00, with discounts for seniors (65+ €4/€6.50), students/minors 6-17 (€4/€6) and free for under-3s.
quote: Adults One-way €5.50 Return €8.00 ... The cable car departs from 'Place Maurice Servais' in the city centre and provides transport up to the Citadelle.

claim: The cable car ride lasts about 4 minutes, crosses the Sambre and reaches 103 m above ground at the citadel esplanade, with panoramic cabin views of the Sambre-Meuse confluence.
quote: The cable car starts from Place Maurice Servais in the historic centre, crosses over the Sambre river and flies towards the walls of the citadels, stopping on an esplanade 650 m further, reaching its culminating point at 103 m above the ground.

claim: The Citadel guided underground tour lasts 90 minutes, covers 495 m of restored galleries with 3D animations and sound, departs from Terra Nova visitor centre and requires advance online booking the day before at the latest.
quote: Reservations (mandatory) are only made on this website at the latest the day before your arrival ... 495 meters of restored underground galleries ... 3D animations, projections and sound effects reinforce and illustrate the guide's narrative.

claim: The Citadel of Namur contains one of the longest networks of underground passages in Europe, with around 350 steps and a constant tunnel temperature of 12-14°C.
quote: the longest underground passages of the Old Continent, which lay within a Citadel, with 350 steps in the visit of underground galleries for a guided tour of more or less 500 meters long. The temperature is 12°c to 14°c in the tunnels.

claim: A Citadelle Pass combining three visits (underground tour, Terra Nova visitor centre and a third site) is sold for €18, useful for a half-day visit.
quote: Citadelle Pass: 3 visits for 18€ in Namur

claim: The Félicien Rops Museum at Rue Fumal 12 is open 10:00-18:00 (last entry 17:00), closed Mondays and on the 3rd weekend of September; €5 standard / €8 with temporary exhibition, free under 12.
quote: From 10 am to 6 pm, last admission at 5 pm. Closed on Mondays. Closed on 24, 25, 31/12, 01/01 and the 3rd weekend in September ... €5 / €8 with the temporary exhibition. Discount for students and senior citizens. Free for children under 12.

claim: TreM.a (Provincial Museum of Ancient Arts of Namur, Rue de Fer 24) houses Middle Ages and Renaissance collections and the Treasure of Oignies; open 10:00-18:00 daily except Mondays, with adult admission €3.
quote: The museum is set up in the Town Hall of Gaiffier d'Hestroy, an 18th century listed house, and presents the Middle Ages and Renaissance collections from the Archaeological Society of Namur, and the extraordinary medieval treasures of the priory of Saint-Nicolas d'Oignies.

claim: The Walloon Parliament, in the former Saint-Gilles Hospice at the foot of the citadel, offers free guided tours (about 1h30) on select Saturdays in 2026 at 9:30, 11:00, 14:00 and 15:30, with group bookings required at least two weeks ahead.
quote: Samedi 27 juin 2026, les horaires sont les suivants : 9h30, 11h, 14h, 15h30 (un groupe par tranche horaire). Les groupes sont composés de minimum 5 et de maximum 30 personnes ... visite dure environ 1h30.

claim: Saint-Aubin's Cathedral on Place Saint-Aubain is an Italianate neoclassical cathedral completed in 1767, with a baroque facade and dome, and houses paintings by Van Dyck, Jordaens and Nicolaï; entry is free.
quote: This vast Italianate neoclassical cathedral, finished in 1767, has an undeniably impressive exterior.

claim: Place d'Armes is the central square of Namur's old town, ringed by cafés and the former commodities exchange (now Palais des Congrès), and features the bronze 'Djoseph èt Françwès' statue of two snail-walking figures - Namur's tongue-in-cheek answer to Laurel and Hardy.
quote: The heart of Namur is Place d'Armes, surrounded by cafes, restaurants, and important buildings such as the former commodities exchange, now the Palais des Congrès. Notable is the monument of bronze figures Djoseph èt Françwès.

claim: Le Grognon is the spit of land at the confluence of the Sambre and Meuse below the citadel; named for its pig-snout shape, it is the medieval heart of Namur and now an open public 'Confluence' esplanade.
quote: The Grognon is the historic heart of the Belgian city of Namur, capital of Wallonia, taking the form of a pointed piece of land at the confluence of the Sambre and Meuse rivers. The shape of the confluence resembles a pig's snout, hence the name Grognon.

claim: Namur en Mai, the festival of fairground/street arts, runs Thursday 14 to Saturday 16 May 2026 across the old town with 130+ performances (circus, concerts, parades), most of them free.
quote: Namur en Mai - Festival des arts forains ... plus de 133 performances, dont beaucoup sont gratuites : cirque, concerts et parades de rue.

claim: Fêtes de Wallonie 2026 run 11-21 September in Namur with the symbolic Stilt Joust on Place Saint-Aubain, mass in Walloon and traditional dances; the festival draws over 250,000 people.
quote: Dates: September 11-21, 2026 ... Sunday afternoon on Place Saint-Aubain: The renowned Stilt Joust ... 'more than 250,000 people' for the weekend festivities.

claim: Floreffe Abbey runs hour-long guided tours of the abbey church April 1 to September 30 (closed Mondays except holidays) at 13h30, 14h30, 16h00 and 17h00 with extra 10h30/11h30 slots in July-August, at €8 per adult; the self-guided exterior tour costs €5 year-round via a guidebook sold at the mill-brewery.
quote: Individual Abbey Church Tours — April 1–September 30 (closed Mondays, except holidays; closed during Espéranzah festival July 24-29). Departure times: 1:30pm, 2:30pm, 4pm, 5pm. July-August additions: 10:30am, 11:30am. Cost: €8.00 per person.

claim: Floreffe is a Premonstratensian abbey founded in 1121 whose old mill-brewery offers daily tastings of abbey beers, cheese and bread, sitting roughly 18 km southwest of Liernu near the Sambre.
quote: Floreffe Abbey, founded in 1121 by Saint Norbert... The old mill-brewery offers tastings of abbey products: beers, bread, and cheeses.

claim: Les Jardins d'Annevoie 2026 admission is €12 adult / €9 student / €8 child (6-17) / free under 6, with a €35 annual pass; visits are self-guided via multilingual leaflet, and guided tours require 15-day-advance booking at €70 per guide for up to 25 people.
quote: Adult Individual: €12 | Group (20+): €11. Student (18-30): €9 individual / €8 group. Child (6-17): €8 individual / €7 group. Child (under 6): Free. Annual pass: €35.

claim: Annevoie's water gardens — Belgium's only surviving 18th-century water gardens — open for a special pre-season window 14 Feb-1 Mar 2026 (€7) and run their main season from 28 March to 11 November 2026.
quote: Une ouverture exceptionnelle est proposée du 14/02 au 01/03 : de 09h30 à 17h00... Une offre est valable du 28/03/2026 au 11/11/2026, selon les horaires d'ouverture réguliers.

claim: The Benedictine Abbaye de Gembloux (~11 km west of Liernu, now the Gembloux Agro-Bio Tech faculty of ULiège) opens for ticketed 90-minute guided tours on only four 2026 summer dates — Sat 11 Jul, Sun 26 Jul, Sat 8 Aug, Sun 23 Aug — at 14h00 for €5 adult / €1 child under 12.
quote: Saturday, July 11 at 2:00 p.m.; Sunday, July 26 at 2:00 p.m.; Saturday, August 8 at 2:00 p.m.; Sunday, August 23 at 2:00 p.m. Summer visits: €5 per person... Children under 12: €1.

claim: Château de Spontin — one of the few Belgian châteaux with an authentic working drawbridge — opens Tue-Sun 10h-17h in July-August and Wed/Sat/Sun 14h-17h in Sept-Oct, with €8 adult / €5 child admission and a strong recommendation to call ahead at +32 451 03 25 20 since private events can close advertised dates.
quote: Juillet & août : Du mardi au dimanche, de 10h à 17h. Septembre, octobre : Mercredi, samedi et dimanche 14h – 17h. Adults: €8. Children (under 12): €5.

claim: Spontin sits in the Bocq valley about 30 km southeast of Liernu — well inside the half-day radius — and its 2026 schedule adds an exceptional opening 27 April–10 May plus the spring half-term holidays.
quote: Le château sera ouvert du 27 avril au 10 mai, puis du 1er au 31 août, du mardi au dimanche de 10h à 17h. Le château sera également ouvert pendant les deux semaines des vacances de printemps de 14h à 17h.

claim: Crupet's Grotte Saint-Antoine de Padoue — a free, always-open 1900-1903 plaster-and-cast-iron tableau famous for its devil scene — draws over 10,000 visitors a year and combines well with a stroll past the Donjon de Carondelet in one of Wallonia's Plus Beaux Villages.
quote: Built between 1900 and 1903... The grotto contains scenes from the life of Saint Anthony, recreated with plaster and cast iron statues, with the devil scene being the most famous. The grotto attracts more than 10,000 visitors per year. Entrance is free.

claim: The 13th-century Donjon de Carondelet of Crupet — restored through 2020 and considered Belgium's best-preserved medieval fortified tower — is private property only opened to the public during Heritage Days in September; for other dates visitors must inquire at the Assesse tourism office.
quote: Le Donjon Carondelet est une propriété privée, il n'est pas visitable, sauf lors des Journées du Patrimoine.

claim: Château de Franc-Waret, a classical 18th-century pile just northeast of Namur on a 1,600-hectare estate with French gardens and an English park, is private and only accessible by prior appointment — making it a fit for chance event bookings, not a drop-in half-day option.
quote: Le château et son magnifique parc sont accessibles uniquement sur rendez-vous... Le domaine de Franc-Waret est entièrement privé.

claim: Maredsous Abbey's guided tours run every Saturday, Sunday and public holiday at 14h00 and 16h00 (15h30 in winter) plus daily during school holidays, at €9 adult / €7.50 senior-student / free under 12, with separate Taste Tour (cheese museum + microbrewery + beer-and-cheese tasting) and Distillery options.
quote: Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays: 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM (3:30 PM in winter). Cost: €9 per person; children under 12 are free; seniors and students pay €7.50.

claim: Maredsous lies in the Molignée valley near Denée roughly 30-33 km south of Liernu — at the outer edge of the 30 km radius — and pairs naturally with the area's draisines and Annevoie gardens for a fuller day out.
quote: Maredsous Abbey... located in the heart of the Molignee Valley... founded in 1872.

claim: The Meuse RAVeL stage Dinant–Namur is 28 km, flat, family-friendly, passes through Wépion and the Annevoie gardens, mostly asphalt with a 3 km dolomite section at Houx lock and some cobblestones from Anhée onward.
quote: follow the Meuse RAVeL along its own path until you reach Namur ... the surface at Houx lock changes from asphalt to fine dolomite rock for three kilometres ... rest area at the Promenade de Meuse

claim: La Meuse à vélo is Wallonia's first fully signposted long-distance cycling route, covering 147 km along the river valley and overlapping EuroVelo 19.
quote: the first long-distance cycling route fully signposted and waymarked in Wallonia, enabling you to cover 147 km following one of Europe's most beautiful river valleys

claim: Les Jardins d'Annevoie open daily 09:30–17:30 in April–June and Sept–Nov, and 09:30–18:30 in July–August, running from 28 March to 11 November 2026; parking €3 for 4 hours.
quote: April to June from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM, July to August from 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM ... open from March 28, 2026 to November 11, 2026 ... charged parking at €3 for 4 hours

claim: Annevoie is the only water garden in Belgium, laid out in the 18th century, mixing French, English and Italian styles.
quote: the only water gardens in Belgium and are among the most beautiful in Europe ... the perspectives of the French style, the whimsy of the English style, and the intimate charm of the Italian style

claim: Wépion's Musée de la Fraise opens Tue–Sun 11:00–18:00 from April to September, with a Fraise'tival strawberry festival on 2 August 2026.
quote: open April to September Tuesday to Sunday from 11am to 6pm ... On August 2, 2026, Fraise'tival

claim: Wépion strawberries are harvested from May (greenhouse) through June (field) and July–October (later plantings), sold at a 19:30 evening auction (Criée de Wépion) throughout the harvest season.
quote: June is meant for unforced and field production. From July to October, harvests from the seedlings bedded out from April to July extend the growing season ... Every evening at 7.30 during the harvest season

claim: Kayak descents on the Lesse with Dinant Evasion run daily from 4 April to 31 October 2026 — 9 km, 12 km (2h30), or 21 km (5h) routes, costing €27–€41/person.
quote: 12 km descents are available every day from April 4, 2026 to October 31, 2026 ... 12 km (2h30) or 21 km (5h)

claim: The Citadel of Namur and Jardin des Senteurs loop is a moderate 6.3 km walk (200 m climb, ~1.5–2 h) along the Meuse and past the citadel's scented garden, recommended in spring.
quote: moderate hike that covers 3.9 miles with an elevation gain of 623 feet ... Jardin des Senteurs, whose gardens house numerous beautiful flowers and are especially highly recommended in the spring

claim: Profondeville offers over 60 km of marked trails in the Haute-Meuse valley, with highlight viewpoints at Rochers de Frêne, Couleuvrine, Sibérie and 'Seven Meuses'.
quote: over 60 kilometres of marked paths in the Profondeville Forest ... viewpoints such as Couleuvrine, Sibérie, and the 'seven Meuses' for splendid panoramas ... Rochers de Frêne Belvedere

claim: The Rochers de Frêne belvedere sits roughly 100 m above the Meuse at Lustin/Profondeville and is one of the best-preserved panoramic viewpoints over the Haute Meuse.
quote: situated a hundred meters above the Meuse, offering some of the best-protected landscapes of the Haute Meuse

claim: Pro Velo Namur rents classic, electric and longtail cargo bikes by the hour, day or month, providing a base for Meuse RAVeL day-rides from the city.
quote: rental of classic bicycles, electric bikes and longtail cargo bikes at competitive rates for a few hours or several months

claim: Lokki offers bike and e-bike rentals in Namur from about €15/day with online booking.
quote: Bike and electric bike rentals in Namur from €15 per day

claim: Liernu has a 7 km / ~2-hour signed loop walk 'La balade sur les terres du Gros Chêne' starting at the village's famed millennial oak.
quote: Liernu - La balade sur les terres du gros chêne ... 7 kilometers long and takes approximately 2 hours

claim: Eghezée's cultural centre Écrin documents the Liernu Gros Chêne walk and other local Hesbaye village balades suitable for half-day outings from the restaurant.
quote: Liernu – la balade sur les terres du gros chêne

claim: Walibi Belgium in Wavre (~22 km north of Liernu) reopens 4 April 2026 and runs through October, with advance tickets from €48 and height-tier pricing (€54 over 1.40 m, €44 for 1–1.40 m).
quote: general admission is €48 per person... €54 for visitors over 1.40m and €44 for those between 1-1.4m

claim: Walibi's new 2026 headline attraction is Mecalodon, a family Gerstlauer launched coaster with three top-hat hills inside the new Dock World themed harbour zone.
quote: Mecalodon is distinguished by its three "Top Hats": hills 14 to 15 meters high... family-oriented multi-launch coaster

claim: Aqualibi, the indoor tropical water park next to Walibi, opens daily 10:00–18:00 (later in school holidays) and recently added a 25-m tower with four slides unique in the Benelux.
quote: imposing 25-meter-high tower from which 4 water slides, unique in the Benelux, originate

claim: Parc Attractif Reine Fabiola, perched on Namur's citadel ~17 km south of Liernu, runs 4 April–1 November 2026 with €4 entry, mini-golf, trampolines, pedal-karts and a reopened renovated track aimed at ages 2.5–12.
quote: officially opens its 2026 season on Saturday, April 4 at 11:00 AM and will remain open until November 1

claim: PARF's 2026 season is anchored by the long-awaited reopening of its go-kart circuit, closed two years for renovation, with police-led road-safety workshops on site.
quote: long-awaited reopening of the circuit track, which was closed for two years for complete renovation

claim: Namur's Citadelle is open daily 10:00–18:00 from 1 April to 27 September 2026, with a 4-activity Citadelle Pass (Terra Nova, tourist train, underground galleries, medieval immersive tour) at €36 adults / €32 reduced.
quote: From April 1 to September 27, the site is open Monday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm... Citadelle Pass 4 activities (4h30) costs €36 for adults

claim: Don't Go Bananas in Gembloux (~12 km west of Liernu) offers an indoor escape room "Avis de recherche en Transylvanie" plus an outdoor escape game, with a second indoor room "Sous les lueurs de l'océan" planned for early 2026; €22–€35 per player.
quote: Plans are in place to start work on a second escape room called "Sous les lueurs de l'océan" in January 2026

claim: EnigmaLock in Namur (Chaussée de Dinant 275) is a 4.8/5-rated escape-game venue, reopened in a new "Maison de l'Alchimiste" building, with prices €25–€40.
quote: EnigmaLock is highly rated at 4.8/5 with prices ranging from 25€ to 40€

claim: Fun Galaxy in Gembloux bundles 8 bowling lanes, a Star-Wars-themed laser tag, 400 m² of free-roaming VR, 25 arcade games, US pool and a 12-hole black-light pirate mini-golf under one roof — ideal rainy-day half-day.
quote: 8 bowling lanes, a 12-hole mini-golf, 25 arcade games, a Laser Game with Star Wars decor, 4 American pool tables, and 400m² of virtual reality exploration

claim: Mini-Golf de Namur in Saint-Servais offers a classic 18-hole outdoor course with cafeteria, ~16 km south of Liernu.
quote: Parcours 18 pistes à Saint-Servais

claim: MusAfrica (the renamed Musée africain de Namur) opens Wednesday–Saturday 10:00–17:00 plus the first Sunday of each month, a 10-minute walk from Namur station.
quote: open from Wednesday to Saturday from 10:00 to 17:00 and the first Sunday of each month

claim: The Musée Félicien Rops in central Namur (devoted to the city's provocative 19th-century engraver) opens Tuesday–Sunday 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:00.
quote: open from 10 am to 6 pm (18h) Tuesday through Sunday, with last admission at 5 pm (17h)

claim: JMKarting Namur in Floreffe (~20 km SW of Liernu) runs a 1,000-m two-level indoor F1-style circuit with Sodikart SR4 270cc karts and 15-minute sessions, plus a kids' play area for ages 3–12.
quote: 2 circuits indoor with "F1" designed tracks... 1,000 meters spread across 2 levels

claim: Domaine provincial de Chevetogne sits at 5590 Chevetogne between Rochefort and Ciney — ~45 km south of Liernu, putting it just outside the 30 km radius despite its appeal as a 600-ha family domain.
quote: located in Namur Province, between Rochefort and Ciney... 5590 Chevetogne

claim: Pairi Daiza zoo (Brugelette) is ~85 km from Namur — well outside a 30 km radius from Liernu — about 1 hr 2 min by car.
quote: The distance between Namur and Pairi Daiza is 53 miles... approximately 1 hour and 2 minutes to drive

claim: The Euro Space Center planetarium/simulator complex is in Transinne (Libin), Luxembourg Province — ~63 km road from Namur, out of range for a Liernu half-day.
quote: Euro Space Center is a science museum and educational tourist attraction located in Transinne (Libin), near Redu

claim: Liernu's own quirky landmark is the Gros Chêne — a millennium-old oak with a 14 m trunk circumference, classified Walloon heritage, with a Brotherhood holding its 47th Chapter on 30 May 2026.
quote: The Gros Chêne is a Grand Venerable oak tree aged more than 1000 years... trunk circumference of 14 meters... 47th Chapter of the Brotherhood of the Gros Chêne de Liernu is being held on Saturday, May 30, 2026

claim: Abbaye de Maredsous in Denée is 21 km SW of Namur — roughly at the 30 km edge from Liernu — and combines abbey visits with cheese, bread, and Trappist-style beer tasting plus family walking trails.
quote: located outside the village of Denée, 21km (13 miles) southwest of Namur... known for making bread, cheese and beer

claim: Domaine du Chenoy in Emines/La Bruyère (a few minutes from Namur) is a 15-hectare organic Walloon vineyard with bookable cellar-and-vineyard tours plus tasting of red and white wines on site (reservation required).
quote: Established in 2003 in Émines, just a few minutes from Namur, this fifteen-hectare vineyard… Certified in organic viticulture… visitors can taste a selection of red and white wines produced on site (reservation required).

claim: Domaine du Chenoy schedules guided visits with tasting on Saturdays at 10:30 and 14:00 from April to October, by reservation.
quote: From April to October, visits are available by reservation on Saturdays at 10:30 and 14:00.

claim: Domaine du Ry d'Argent in Bovesse (Rue de la Distillerie 51) farms 13 hectares of vines at 160 m altitude and produces white, rosé, red and traditional-method sparkling wines.
quote: Domaine du Ry d'Argent | vignoble belgique | Rue de la Distillerie 51, Bovesse 5081 La Bruyere, Belgium

claim: Ry d'Argent hosts a free monthly open tasting on the first Friday of the month 17:30–19:30 (no reservation) plus by-appointment guided cellar visits with a 4-wine tasting.
quote: tasting each first Friday of the month, from 17:30 to 19:30, where the winemaker selects three wines in harmony with the season. Entrance is free and no reservation is needed.

claim: The Floreffe abbey beer range (Blonde, Double, Triple, Prima Melior) has been brewed under licence by Brasserie Lefebvre in Quenast since 1983, not at the abbey itself.
quote: In 1983, the Lefebvre Brewery took over production of Floreffe beers. The Floreffe range includes Blonde, Double, Floreffe Triple and Prima Melior.

claim: Maredsous beers have been brewed under licence by Duvel Moortgat since 1963; a 2016 on-site Cheesemaking Museum lets visitors see milk turned into cheese and the cheese matured.
quote: Since 1963 the Maredsous abbey beers have been brewed, under licence, by Duvel Moortgat… In 2016 the Cheesemaking Museum was opened, where visitors can see how milk is transformed into cheese and how the cheese is matured.

claim: Namur's relocated Saturday Marché du Bord de l'Eau runs along Boulevard Frère Orban beside the Sambre, with scenic views of the Citadelle, accessible by bus, electric shuttle and the University car park.
quote: the new site offers 'better accessibility, with the University car park, bus and electric shuttle stops' nearby… The venue provides scenic views overlooking the Citadelle and the Sambre river.

claim: Gembloux's weekly market falls on Friday and carries fruit and veg, butchers, cheese, Italian specialties, bakeries, fishmongers, organic and dairy producers (not Saturday).
quote: There is a market in Gembloux held on Fridays that features fruits and vegetables, butcheries, delicatessens, cheeses, Italian specialties, bakeries, pastries, fish shops…

claim: Belgian chocolatier Galler — Liège-founded — runs one of its 14 boutiques in Namur for tablets, pralines and ballotins.
quote: Galler, a Liège-based company, is an international reference in the chocolate world, with one of its 14 boutiques located in Namur.

claim: Thomas Manini is a Namur artisan chocolatier producing his own pralines, shortbread, spreads and jams in-shop.
quote: Thomas Manini is a chocolatier in Namur offering artisan chocolates, shortbread, spreads, and jams made with passion and expertise.

claim: Musée de la Fraise opens Tue–Sun 11:00–18:00 from April to September (Tue–Fri 13:00–17:00 off-season), aligning with prime Wépion strawberry months.
quote: April to September: Tuesday to Sunday from 11:00 AM to 6:00 PM. October to March: Tuesday to Friday from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

claim: Escargotière de Warnant in Anhée breeds about 600,000–800,000 snails per year and runs guided tours with tasting on Saturdays at 16:00 from 1 April–30 November, daily 14–18h in July/August.
quote: Tours can be taken from April 1st to November 30th every Saturday at 4 pm, and in July and August you can visit Tuesday-Sunday between 2pm-6pm.

claim: La Chèvre et le Chou in Waret-la-Chaussée (Eghezée, Rue du Culot 55) runs a farm shop Thu 14–18h and Fri–Sat 10–18h selling their goat cheeses (e.g. 'Goutte de Waret') and organic vegetables, with goat-milking experiences.
quote: You can find their products at the farm shop on Thursdays from 2-6 PM, and Fridays and Saturdays from 10 AM-6 PM… visitors can milk a goat at the farm

claim: Brasserie du Bocq, an independent family brewery in Purnode-Yvoir since 1858 (brewer of Gauloise, Blanche de Namur, Saint-Benoît, Triple Moine), currently no longer runs public visitor tours after its facility upgrade.
quote: Currently, the brewery no longer organises tourist visits to the Brewery due to their new facilities.

claim: L'Air du Temps itself sits in 5 hectares of land at Liernu, half cultivated, growing about 400 vegetable, fruit and herb species that supply roughly 90% of the restaurant's plant produce.
quote: the restaurant L'air du temps is surrounded by 5 hectares of land, half of which is cultivated and produces 90% of the supplies of vegetables, fruits and herbs required by the restaurant.

claim: La Biscuiterie Namuroise in Jemeppe-sur-Sambre revives 1908 family recipes for moques and pepper biscuits — a regional sweet-stop within easy range of Liernu.
quote: This biscuitery uses recipes inspired by 1908 from one of the founders' grandfather, and offers a variety of biscuits including their famous 'moques' and pepper biscuits.

claim: L'Air du Temps address is Rue de la Croix Monet 2, 5310 Liernu (Éghezée), Namur Province.
quote: L'AIR DU TEMPS - Rue de la Croix Monet 2, Liernu, Namur, Belgium - Modern European

claim: L'Air du Temps holds Two MICHELIN Stars in the 2026 Belgium Guide plus a Green Star, set in a white farmstead built around a square courtyard in the fields of Liernu.
quote: Two Stars Excellent cooking restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Belgium ... beautiful white farmstead built around a square courtyard in the fields of Liernu

claim: The restaurant is closed Monday and Tuesday and priced in the €€€€ tier (high-end fine dining); reservations via +32 81 81 30 48.
quote: closing days: Monday and Tuesday ... €€€€ category, indicating a high-end fine dining establishment ... Phone: 081.81.30.48

claim: L'Air du Temps offers 11 on-site bedrooms at an average official double-room rate around €210 including breakfast; rooms must be vacated by 11:00.
quote: The average official price for a double room including breakfast is €210 ... Breakfast is served from 8:30 to 10:00 at €25 per person ... Rooms must be vacated by 11:00 the next morning.

claim: L'Air du Temps is ranked #1 of the B&Bs in Éghezée on Tripadvisor, with breakfast included and described as outstanding and hearty.
quote: Outstanding breakfast ... very original and hearty ... ranked #1 of 3 B&Bs in Eghezee

claim: Liernu to Namur is 16.2 km / ~13 min by car; TEC bus line 822 takes 31 min from Liernu Village to Namur Omalius but runs only every 4 hours.
quote: Distance: 16.2 km ... Time: Approximately 13 minutes ... Line 822 bus ... Duration: 31 minutes ... Frequency: Every 4 hours

claim: Liernu to Wavre (gateway to Walibi) is 29.1 km / about 20 min by car.
quote: The driving distance between Liernu to Wavre is 29 km. It takes approximately 20 min to drive from Liernu to Wavre.

claim: Liernu to Annevoie-Rouillon (Les Jardins d'Annevoie) is 34 km / about 32 min by car — just outside the 30-km radius but reachable in a half-day.
quote: The driving distance between Liernu to Annevoie-Rouillon is 34 km. It takes approximately 32 min to drive from Liernu to Annevoie-Rouillon.

claim: Liernu to Gembloux is 11.8 km / about 13 min by car; TEC line 71 covers it in ~16 min from Aische-en-Refail but only every 4 hours.
quote: Distance: 11.8 km ... Time: Approximately 13 minutes ... Line 71 ... Duration: 16 minutes ... Departure: AISCHE-EN-REFAIL Pont des Dames ... Every 4 hours

claim: Liernu to Floreffe (Abbey) is 20.3 km / about 20 min by car.
quote: the road distance is 20.3 km between the two locations ... The journey takes approximately 20 minutes by car

claim: Liernu has no scheduled bus stop; villagers use the TEC on-demand 'Liernu-Corbeau' Flexitec service, so visitors without a car effectively need a taxi.
quote: Residents of Liernu can use the TEC on-demand transport service via the Liernu-Corbeau stop located in the Corbeau district ... optimized and collective trips along the Gembloux/Sombreffe axis

claim: The Citadel of Namur site is open daily 10:00–18:00 with the cable car also running 10:00–18:00 on weekends — a clean Saturday-afternoon fit before driving back to Liernu.

claim: Late spring weather around Namur averages 9–19 °C in May and 12–20 °C in June with ~11 rainy days; pack a light layer plus waterproof for garden visits.
